summary: This rewrite stage is sound and targets the right bottleneck: full verify_16/32 sits on paired FA3 at about 2.2 TB/s and 2.3-2.6x its floor, and it is DIAGNOSIS action 1(b). Its smem arithmetic is wrong, though. STAGES_WG=6 cannot hold 2 CTAs/SM next to s5's non-ring smem, so the builder must size the ring from s5's real layout (STAGES_WG=4) before building. The gate should use the new two-round lesson.
justification: Mechanism (A). s5 (71e40388) was correct but slow: 288.7 vs 164.4 us at B=16 and 429.5 vs 302.4 at B=32. Its pipeline puts a CTA-wide EMPTY rendezvous (256 arrivals across BOTH warpgroups) behind a fully serial S->transpose->softmax->PV chain. Giving each kv-head warpgroup its own ring with 128-arrival barriers is a plausible way to decouple the two warpgroups, so 4 independent warpgroups per SM can hide each other's chain latency. OVL=1 (wait_group 1 over a second S accumulator) is the standard FA3 ILP answer. The compute budget in DIAGNOSIS fits under the gather: about 21 us of FP8 wgmma and 40 us of MUFU against a 108 us gather at 3 TB/s. The master decode kernel already reaches 3.0 TB/s on the same page-1 gather, so M2 (verify_16 <=135, verify_32 <=255 us) is physically reachable, and M3 (<=115/<=225) is decode parity. The expected rows match TASK.md: full verify_16/32 weight 16, floors 63.4/126.8 us; FINDINGS profile 148.7 FA3 + 6.4 combine + 3.1 prepare of a 162.5 us shape, and 288.7 + 6.7 of 302.0. verify_1, decode and sliding stay flat because the gate covers only 1<B and window==0. The prior is correct and the difference is real: s5 is the same math with a CTA-wide ring and no overlap, and ws-s1 uses a 128-thread producer at 1 CTA/SM. It is not on the do-not-try list: that list bans mma.sync verify and single-warp bulk gathers, and this kernel is wgmma with all threads issuing loads. CONCRETE DEFECT: the smem budget claim '2 x 6 x 8 KB = 96 KB, under s5's 99936 B, so 2 CTAs/SM holds' is wrong. s5 has STAGES=4, so its ring is only 64 KB of the 99936 B. The other 34400 B are VT 16 KB, IDX 8 KB, QS 8 KB, seq/pre/bar/flag about 1.4 KB, and the 1 KB alignment slack. 2 CTAs/SM allows at most about 115.7 KB of dynamic smem per CTA (228 KB per SM, 1 KB reserved per CTA), which leaves about 81.3 KB for the ring: STAGES_WG=4 (64 KB), not 6. A 96 KB ring makes about 130.6 KB, so occupancy silently drops to 1 CTA/SM, and the 'keeps s5's occupancy' premise fails. The SW128 fallback at 'STAGES_WG 3' (2 x 3 x 16 KB = 96 KB) is over budget in the same way. OVL=1 at 12 stages (196608 + 34400 = 231008 B against the 232448 B per-block limit) only just fits; check the printed CTAs/SM. A better fallback than the half-filled rings, and arguably a better primary because it needs no new SWIZZLE_64B descriptor: keep s5's exact 4-stage SW128 128-B-row ring and descriptors, and give each logical 64-B head half of a stage its own FULL_w/EMPTY_w barrier pair. Each warpgroup then fills and frees only its own (swizzled, disjoint) chunks of each stage slot. WEAKEST LINK: the latency-bound reading of s5. A serial per-tile chain should scale about 2x with 2x the tiles, but s5 scaled 1.49x. A linear fit T = a + b*tiles gives a ~148 us component that does not depend on B (b about 1.85 us per tile per CTA at a 2xSM grid). If that fixed part is in the segment start (page-index fill), the Q staging or the ticket epilogue and combine waits, removing the per-tile rendezvous will not touch it. The gather-only DIAG separates producer issue rate from compute, but as written it drops nothing that would expose a fixed cost. A second risk: the split ring makes each warp-wide cp.async cover 8 tokens' 64-B halves instead of 4 tokens' 128-B rows, which doubles the distinct lines per instruction, and the two warpgroups fetch the two halves of each 128-B line at different times. The issue rate or L2/DRAM efficiency could fall below s5's. The gather-only DIAG catches this, which justifies it.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing + paired-heads-launch-cleanup + paired-heads-launch-cleanup-ab-tune-batch-gate: these define the incumbent at full verify 1<B (paired FA3, prepare, combine and _paired_norm_gate_kernel). The prepare gate must time exactly master 5d528bf3's paired path, pre-attention included on both sides, or the 1.05x routing decision is mis-anchored. This is not a confounder of the new kernel's own time.

fused-preattention-triton (+ v3 fused prologue in restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn): it emits the FP8 q (paired/padded layout on full batched layers when paired=True) that the s6 kernel reads. If master's pre-attention for full verify 1<B differs from the 52ca902 base s5 was rebased onto, a layout mismatch shows up as a self-check fallback. That would be misread as the split ring failing. Port against master's actual PAIRED flag for this band.

BEST.json is branch code (combo-b1-chain-c320-fused-pre-pdl, 1.5295), not master (sliding-decode1-cluster-per-kvhead). The headline of a run on master differs from BEST by the decode-side B=1 chain regardless of s6, so judge on the full verify_16/32 top_kernels and the PATH CHOSEN lines, not the headline.
interference: No companions. This is kind: rewrite, and its readout is the replaced kernels' own time on full verify_16/32 plus the in-run PATH CHOSEN and gather-only DIAG lines. Those lines already separate the hypotheses one run could confuse: producer issue-bound (gather-only of each ring), TLP vs ILP (OVL=0 vs OVL=1), and old ring vs split ring (s5's CTA-wide ring timed in the same DIAG). An ab-revert of a landed hypothesis would not help, because the new path is disjoint from every landed kernel except the q layout it consumes, which the self-check covers. Better spending than a companion: in the same prepare DIAG, (1) time the full s5/s6 kernels at two or three B (8/16/32, or a length sweep) and print the fitted fixed component a and per-tile slope b; (2) give the gather-only instantiation the ticket epilogue kept and removed. Together these attribute the ~148 us non-scaling part that the split ring may not address, and tell the next stage what to fix.
rules_flags: Gate statistics: a single interleaved round at >=1.05x goes against the new LESSONS gate (line 27: two interleaved rounds, both >=1.03, candidate IQR <=1.5x master's). Use two rounds with both >=1.05 (or both >=1.03 plus the IQR bound), so a mis-route cannot put an unproven kernel on the judged rows. This is a correctness-of-measurement issue, not a rule breach.

Import/compile clock: 222 s already over 4 modules, and this adds a 5th with at least OVL0, OVL1, three GATHER_ONLY instantiations and any ticket/DBG variants inside a 15-minute run. A load_inline compile cannot be interrupted in-process without threads or extra processes. The 'own deadline' must be an elapsed-time check BEFORE starting the build, falling back to master paired FA3 if it would overrun. Consider compiling the gather-only DIAG instantiations only for this check stage.

The prepare-time DIAG and gate run only on synthetic data and are never called from kernel_fn. That matches prior accepted practice, but keep _WG_BANDS a config-only decision and make sure no module global holds pointers into a judge state (the two-state replay check covers this).

Every key attended: the stream-K tiles must still cover every key of each request's full context. The split ring changes only who loads which half of each row, so no rule issue as long as the bisect table (incl. mid-request 1-tile segments, B1-2t..34t) passes per variant.
open_questions: Does the builder size STAGES_WG from s5's real non-ring smem (34400 B)? STAGES_WG=4 at 2 CTAs/SM, and the printed CTAs/SM line must say 2 for OVL=0, or the run measures 1-CTA/SM TLP and the premise is untested.

What is s5's fixed, B-independent time component (~148 us by a two-point linear fit)? Is it the ticket epilogue/combine spin, the per-segment page-index fill, or Q staging? The split ring does not remove it.

Does the split ring's per-warp access pattern (8 half-lines per cp.async instruction, halves of each 128-B line fetched at different times by the two warpgroups) lower the gather-only TB/s compared with s5's CTA-wide ring? If so, the shared-slot design (s5's SW128 ring with per-half barriers) keeps full-line coalescing while still decoupling the barriers.

Does OVL=1 at 1 CTA/SM fit within 232448 B with 12 stages and no spill (+32 regs over 127 at 256 threads leaves room under 255, but check local bytes)? Would STAGES_WG 10 give more margin with no loss?

The gate times only B=16 (band 2..24) and B=32 (25..64). Small-B rows inside the band (correctness tests B=2 ctx 100000, B=4 ctx 6000) are correctness-only, but confirm that the gate predicate excludes page_size 64 and the dp heads that s5's kernel does not support.
